parsed_output.refined_idea: Test whether providing personalized meal suggestions based on users' existing pantry items and their approximate expiration dates reduces food waste among individuals cooking for one or two people.
parsed_output.core_mechanism: Personalized meal suggestion engine that uses user-provided pantry inventory and estimated expiration dates to generate recipes for one- or two-person meals.
parsed_output.core_mechanism_justification: The mechanism directly fulfills the human intention to influence behavior through tailored suggestions without adding speculative technologies; it relies on data the user is willing to supply, keeping the solution simple and privacy-respectful.

accepted_changes.proposal: Require explicit manual entry of pantry items and expiration dates rather than automated scanning
accepted_changes.promotion_reason: Keeps the solution aligned with the user's explicit willingness to share data and avoids model-generated assumptions
accepted_changes.evidence_or_decision_basis: User interviews indicated preference for manual entry over camera use

candidate_possibilities: AI-driven visual pantry scanner where users snap a photo of their fridge/shelf to extract ingredients and expiration dates
Gamified suggestion platform that awards points/badges for preparing recommended meals and logging leftovers
Integration with smart kitchen devices (RFID containers or barcode scanners) that automatically sync ingredient inventories and expiration dates

rejected_changes.reason_rejected: Introduces incentive bias and relies on self-reported waste, which conflicts with the goal of unbiased behavior measurement
Requires additional hardware that many target users do not own, raising adoption barriers

remaining_uncertainties: Accuracy and completeness of user-provided pantry data
Methods for reliably measuring actual food waste reduction
User willingness to follow suggested meals consistently
Privacy implications of storing pantry inventories
Potential misestimation of ingredient expiration dates
known_risks: User fatigue from manual data entry
Inaccurate self-reporting of waste leading to misleading results
Technical challenges if future visual scanner is added later
Reward system could attract users motivated by points rather than waste reduction
parsed_output.recommended_next_step: Develop a minimal viable product that lets users manually input pantry items and expiration dates, generates personalized meal suggestions, and runs a short pilot study collecting self-reported waste data while monitoring privacy compliance.
